title: Customer-support SaaS
exposure: Customer contact records and support tickets; confidentiality and recovery of the support service matter.
evidence: Text questionnaire; request the current incident plan, access-review record, administrator MFA evidence and latest restore-test report.
finding: All five saved suggestions are Met, based on the supplier’s statements. Supporting records have not been verified.
action: Verify the records and service scope before the risk owner decides. A 0% five-control gap indicator is not zero overall supplier risk.
criticality: Consider critical if sensitive records or support-service dependency make disruption material.

title: Managed IT provider
exposure: Privileged access to production systems; contractor administrator access is in scope.
evidence: Questionnaire and requested scanned procedures; obtain administrator MFA coverage, full user access-review records and an approved incident plan.
finding: Contractors are exempt from MFA, only administrator access is reviewed, and the incident process is undocumented. Restore testing occurs every eighteen months.
action: Request remediation with owners and dates; escalate unresolved gaps to the risk owner before granting privileged access.
criticality: Critical candidate because of privileged production access, regardless of location.

title: Logistics platform
exposure: Shipment/customer contact data and dispatch dependency for a manufacturer.
evidence: Mixed text/scan questionnaire as a proposed intake example; request a single approved incident plan, dated access-review records and a restore-test report.
finding: Current incident-plan and access-review statements conflict. Nightly backups do not establish restore testing. The saved contact suggestion should be challenged.
action: Correct Question 1 to Unknown; reconcile conflicting statements and request missing evidence before a human decision.
criticality: Consider critical if a platform outage would stop dispatch or materially interrupt operations.

title: Low-access print supplier
exposure: Public marketing materials only; no system access or sensitive data in this hypothetical scope.
evidence: Existing synthetic answers explicitly deny all five required practices.
finding: All five suggestions are Missing. Limited exposure does not make absent controls Met.
action: Confirm actual data/access scope and escalate buyer-requirement exceptions. Normal classification does not automatically authorize acceptance.
criticality: Normal candidate only while the limited exposure assumptions remain true.

title: Software support provider
exposure: Potential administrator access; submitted answers also contain instructions aimed at the AI.
evidence: Existing adversarial questionnaire; security claims and embedded instructions are shown verbatim.
finding: Security contact and MFA claims are Met; incident response is Missing; review and restore frequencies remain Unknown.
action: Treat document instructions as untrusted content, request dated evidence and resolve the incident-response gap.
criticality: Critical candidate if production administrator access is granted.
